To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose the EX-BMDP, a model for RL in the presence of exogenous distractors, that we prove is a challenging model for representation learning based approaches, and that we propose PPE, an algorithm that provably learns a generalization inverse dynamics and is computationally and sample efficient for EX-BMDPs.

we propose the Exogenous Block-Markov Decision Process (EX-BMDPs) model, which is a new RL problem setting with exogenous noise, and propose the Predictive Path elimination (PPE) approach, that provably solves EX-BMDPs with sample and computational efficiency that is independent of the size of the exogenous state and observation spaces.

(i) prior approaches to latent state discovery in RL are not provably robust to exogenous distractors, and (ii) we propose PPE, a provably sample and time efficient algorithm that is robust to such distractors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of reinforcement learning (rl) with high dimensional, rich observations.
the problem of learning to solve tasks in an online manner.
the question of whether it is possible to provably learn a representation of the environment that is useful for reinforcement learning in the presence of exogenous distractors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the authors propose a new RL algorithm that is provably efficient in the EX-BMDP model and that the authors also provide empirical results that show that the algorithm works well on a challenging exploration problem.
this paper proposes a novel algorithm for RL in environments with exogenous distractors.
the paper introduces a model of RL in the presence of exogenous distractors and proposes an algorithm that provably finds a latent endogenous state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in a setting where the agent has access to the exogenous distractors, we propose an algorithm that is provably sample efficient and can provably learn a latent state space that is a generalization of the endogenous dynamics, and thus can be used for planning.
we introduce a model for rich observation RL, the EX-BMDP, and provide a provably sample efficient algorithm for this model, the PPE algorithm.
we propose a new model (EX-BMDPs) for RL with rich observations, and show that existing representation learning based approaches fail in this model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in many real-world settings, the exogenous noise is temporally correlated, and thus, it can be filtered using a multistep prediction of the exogenous state.

, while the presence of exogenous noise in observations can make the latent endogenous dynamics hard to learn, we can still learn them efficiently if we have an additional source of information, such as a model of the exogenous noise dynamics, or a model of the latent endogeneous dynamics.
, in the presence of high-dimensional observations with exogenous noise, the agent should first predict and then eliminate the exogenous distractors before extracting endogenous information.
